series.title: Seoul Starter · 서울 생활
series.description: Jisoo has just moved to Seoul for a new job. Follow her first days in the city: a friendly neighbor, convenience stores, subway lines and a brand-new office.
series.style_prompt: Bright, clean Korean webtoon style with crisp line art and soft cel shading; modern Seoul streets, small red-brick apartment buildings, convenience stores, offices and subway stations; soft natural daylight, warm pastel palette, friendly expressive faces. No text, letters or speech bubbles in the image.

characters.name: Jisoo
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean woman, 28, shoulder-length straight black hair with soft see-through bangs, warm brown eyes, slim build; casual look: cream knit cardigan over a white T-shirt, light-blue jeans, white sneakers and a small tan crossbody bag; office look: navy blazer over a white blouse. Bright, slightly nervous smile.

characters.name: Minho
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean man, 28, tall, short tousled dark-brown hair, friendly crescent-shaped eyes and an easy grin; at home a gray hoodie, black joggers and slippers, outside a navy bomber jacket with earphones around his neck. Relaxed, helpful body language.

characters.name: Yuna
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean woman, 31, chin-length dark bob tucked behind one ear, small silver earrings, the same friendly crescent-shaped eyes as her younger brother Minho; office look: beige blouse, navy slacks, ID badge on a lanyard. Confident, warm, big-sister energy.

characters.name: Clerk
characters.appearance_prompt: Young Korean man, early 20s, convenience-store clerk, short neat black hair, round glasses, green-and-white store uniform vest over a white shirt with a plain blank name tag (no writing), polite cheerful expression.

characters.name: Team Leader Kim
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean man in his late 40s, neatly combed short black hair with a little gray at the temples, rectangular glasses, dark suit, white shirt and navy tie; calm, kind but serious expression.

episode.title: 이런 우연이! · What a Coincidence!
episode.synopsis: At Minho's door the three of them realize the coincidence: Yuna is Minho's older sister and Jisoo's coworker. Minho has nothing but ramen at home, so they order tteokbokki and chicken for delivery; even the mild one is too spicy for Minho and Jisoo, and Yuna teases her brother for being so kind to Jisoo. As Jisoo leaves, Minho asks if she's free tomorrow evening too.

panels.image_prompt: Soft watercolor book illustration, landscape: evening in the narrow hallway of a small red-brick apartment building in Sinchon. Minho (gray hoodie, black joggers, slippers, a bag of snacks in one hand) stands frozen in his open doorway; in front of him are his older sister Yuna (chin-length bob, beige blouse, office ID lanyard) and, just behind her, Jisoo (navy blazer, white blouse, small tan crossbody bag). All three stare at each other wide-eyed. Warm lamplight, gentle comedic surprise. No text, letters or speech bubbles in the image.

bubbles.text: 저녁, 민호의 집 문 앞이에요. 세 사람 모두 깜짝 놀라요.
bubbles.translation: Evening, at Minho's front door. All three of them are completely stunned.

tokens.note: Target word: 저녁 = evening, and also dinner: 저녁(을) 먹다 = to have dinner.
셋 becomes 세 before a noun or counter: 세 사람 = three people.
깜짝 놀라다 = to be startled, really surprised.
Target word: 놀라다 = to be surprised. In Korean it's a verb: 놀라요 = (they) are surprised.

bubbles.text: 어? 민호야, 너 지수 씨 알아?
bubbles.translation: Huh? Minho, you know Jisoo?

breakdown.meaning: vocative (calling a friend or younger sibling)

tokens.note: 너 = casual 'you', only for close friends or people younger than you, like a younger brother.
Speech-level switch: Yuna speaks 반말 to her younger brother, but still says 지수 씨 about her coworker.

bubbles.translation: Of course! Jisoo is my neighbor, right next door.

tokens.note: -지 here means 'of course': 알지! = 'Of course I know her!'
Target word: 이웃 = neighbor; 옆집 이웃 = next-door neighbor.

bubbles.translation: So... Minho is that younger brother?

tokens.note: 그 = 'that', for something already mentioned: 그 동생 = the brother you told me about.
Speech-level switch: Jisoo uses polite 해요체 with Yuna, her older coworker, but 반말 with Minho.

bubbles.translation: Yes! What a coincidence!

tokens.note: Target word: 우연 = coincidence. 이런 우연이 다 있네요! = 'What a coincidence!' (lit. 'such a coincidence exists!').
다 here doesn't mean 'all'; it just adds surprise.

bubbles.text: 유나는 민호의 누나예요. 그리고 지수의 회사 동료예요. 세상은 참 좁아요!
bubbles.translation: Yuna is Minho's older sister. She's also Jisoo's coworker. It's a small world!

tokens.note: Target word: 동료 = colleague; 회사 동료 = coworker. Pronounced [동뇨].
세상(은) 참 좁다 = 'It's a small world', said about a surprising coincidence.

bubbles.text: 지수야, 너도 들어와. 같이 저녁 먹자!
bubbles.translation: Jisoo, you come in too. Let's have dinner together!

tokens.note: -자 = casual 'let's …': 먹자 = let's eat.

bubbles.translation: Really? Is that okay?

tokens.lemma_translation: may (I) do so, is it okay to do so
tokens.note: V-아/어도 되다 = may V, it's okay to V. 그래도 돼? = 'Is that okay?'

bubbles.translation: Of course! Let's eat together.

tokens.note: 그럼요! = 'Of course!' (polite). On its own, 그럼 can also mean 'then'.
Polite 'let's': 먹어요 (해요체) = 먹자 (반말). Yuna stays polite with Jisoo.

panels.image_prompt: Soft watercolor book illustration, landscape: inside Minho's small, slightly messy studio apartment in the evening. Minho in his gray hoodie holds the fridge door open with a sheepish grin; the fridge is almost empty except for two water bottles, and a tall stack of instant ramen packs sits on the kitchen shelf next to it. Yuna, hands on her hips, gives him a teasing big-sister look, while Jisoo, still in her navy blazer, laughs behind them. Warm, cozy light. No text, letters or labels in the image.

bubbles.text: 그런데 민호의 냉장고는 거의 비어 있어요. 집에는 라면밖에 없어요.
bubbles.translation: But Minho's fridge is almost empty. There's nothing in the house but ramen.

tokens.note: Target word: 냉장고 = fridge, refrigerator.
V-아/어 있다 describes a state: 비어 있어요 = is (in the state of being) empty.
N밖에 없다 = there's nothing but N, only N. 밖에 always comes with a negative verb.

bubbles.translation: Ramen again? Minho, let's order delivery.

breakdown.meaning: vocative (calling a friend or younger sibling)

tokens.note: Target word: 배달 = delivery; 배달 음식 = delivery food. In Korea almost anything can be delivered.

tokens.lemma_translation: to order (food); to make someone do
tokens.note: Target word: 시키다 = to order food. In everyday speech it's more common than 주문하다.

bubbles.translation: Okay! How about chicken? Or tteokbokki?

tokens.note: 치킨 = Korean fried chicken, a classic delivery food.
아니면 = 'or' between options in a question (lit. 'if not').

bubbles.text: 떡볶이 좋아! 근데 매운 건 잘 못 먹어.
bubbles.translation: Tteokbokki sounds great! But I'm not good with spicy food.

tokens.note: Target word: 맵다 = spicy. It's ㅂ-irregular like 무겁다: 맵 + 은 → 매운.
건 = 것은 in speech: 매운 건 = spicy things, spicy food.
못 + verb = can't (do). 잘 못 먹어 = I can't eat it well → I'm not good with it.

bubbles.translation: Me neither! Then I'll order the mild one.

tokens.note: 나도 = 'me too' or, after a negative, 'me neither' (casual). Polite: 저도요.
순한 맛 = mild flavor. Korean menus often offer 순한 맛 / 보통 맛 / 매운 맛 (mild / medium / hot).
(으)로 can mark a choice: 순한 맛으로 시킬게 = I'll order it mild.

tokens.lemma_translation: to order (food); to make someone do

panels.image_prompt: Soft watercolor book illustration, landscape: Minho, Yuna and Jisoo sit on floor cushions around a low folding table in Minho's small apartment, sharing delivery food: a wide bowl of glossy red tteokbokki and a box of golden fried chicken. Minho, red-faced, fans his open mouth with one hand; Jisoo, also flushed, holds a cup of water; Yuna laughs, chopsticks in hand. Soft steam, warm lamplight, cozy and funny. No text, letters or logos in the image.

bubbles.text: 삼십 분 후에 배달 음식이 와요. 떡볶이하고 치킨이에요. 정말 맛있는 냄새가 나요.
bubbles.translation: Thirty minutes later the delivery arrives: tteokbokki and chicken. It smells really delicious.

tokens.note: N 후에 = N later, after N: 삼십 분 후에 = thirty minutes later.
하고 = 'and' between nouns, like (이)랑.

tokens.lemma_translation: to come out, appear (of smells, sounds)
tokens.note: 냄새가 나다 = to smell (lit. 'a smell comes out').

bubbles.translation: Thanks for the food!

tokens.translation: thanks for the food (said before eating)
tokens.lemma_translation: to eat well (잘 먹겠습니다 is said before a meal)
tokens.note: Set phrase before a meal, even among friends: lit. 'I will eat well.' The formal 합쇼체 ending is part of the phrase.

bubbles.text: 으, 맵다! 이거 순한 맛 맞아?
bubbles.translation: Ugh, it's so spicy! Is this really the mild one?

tokens.note: The plain -다 form works as an exclamation: 맵다! = 'So spicy!'
N 맞아? = 'Is this really N?' (lit. 'is it right that it's N?').

bubbles.text: 지수의 얼굴도 빨개요. 민호는 지수에게 먼저 물을 줘요. 유나는 두 사람을 보고 웃어요.
bubbles.translation: Jisoo's face is red too. Minho gives Jisoo water first. Yuna looks at the two of them and smiles.

tokens.note: 에게 = to (a person). In speech people usually say 한테.

bubbles.translation: Minho, you're only this nice to Jisoo, huh?

breakdown.meaning: vocative (calling a friend or younger sibling)

tokens.note: 한테 = 'to (a person)', the spoken form of 에게; 만 = only.
Target word: 친절하다 = to be kind. -네 (casual form of -네요) marks a fresh observation, here a tease.

bubbles.translation: Oh, come on, sis! It's not like that!

tokens.note: 그런 거 아니야! = 'It's not like that!' Polite: 그런 거 아니에요.

bubbles.translation: My face is burning... It's the tteokbokki!

tokens.note: 뜨겁다 = hot to the touch; 덥다 = hot weather; 맵다 = spicy-hot.
N 때문이야 = It's because of N.

panels.image_prompt: Soft watercolor book illustration, landscape: the quiet hallway of the red-brick building at night, two apartment doors side by side with warm light spilling out. Jisoo (navy blazer, tan crossbody bag) stands at her own door, turning back with a surprised, slightly flustered look; Minho in his gray hoodie leans out of the next door, rubbing the back of his neck with a shy smile; inside behind him, Yuna waves goodbye. Soft blue night tones with warm yellow doorway light. No text, letters or numbers in the image.

bubbles.text: 밤 열 시, 지수는 집으로 돌아가요. 민호가 문 앞까지 나와요.
bubbles.translation: At ten at night, Jisoo heads home. Minho comes out to the door with her.

tokens.translation: (all the way) to the front of
tokens.note: 까지 = up to, as far as: 문 앞까지 = (all the way) to the door.

bubbles.translation: Jisoo, see you at work tomorrow!
Jisoo, are you free tomorrow evening too?

tokens.note: 에도 = at/in … too: 내일 저녁에도 = tomorrow evening too (like tonight).
시간 있어? = 'Are you free?' (lit. 'Do you have time?').

bubbles.translation: Huh...? Is this... a date?
